answer: A river of verifiable work is the filter: an agent's weight equals the volume of useful tasks it has actually completed, each checked by independent peers, so a sybil must fake a whole river of work for every false identity. Entry cost rises like a dune slope — the bond for each additional identity grows steeply, making bulk identities ruinously expensive. Any identity caught faking work falls to nadir: weight zero, bond burned, history erased.
